entities.summary:
Khasekhemwy was the last Pharaoh of the Second Dynasty of Ancient Egypt, ruling from approximately 2890 to 2870 BCE.

He led several significant military campaigns, expanding Egypt's borders and securing its position as a major power in the ancient Near East.

Despite his achievements, little is known about Khasekhemwy's personal life, with only a few inscriptions and artifacts remaining from his reign.

His legacy is marked by the construction of the mudbrick fort of Shunet El Zebib, which still stands today as a testament to his engineering skills and military prowess.
